title: Doctors and nurses, not AI, must perform medicine under new state law
key_facts: California Assembly Bill 1979, signed by Gov. Gavin Newsom and taking effect on 1 Jan (2027), bars hospitals and doctors' offices from using AI to independently perform medical tasks that require a professional license, such as prescribing medications or ordering tests.

It requires healthcare facilities to take reasonable steps so licensed professionals can exercise independent judgment when AI tools help guide care; clinicians may still use the tools to inform decisions, and AI may still be used for documentation and communication.

Assemblymember Mia Bonta carried the bill, which was sponsored by the California Nurses Association; the hospital association and the California Medical Association (50,000 doctors) were neutral, after the wording was narrowed.

The nurses' union says employers are already putting AI into work nurses and physicians used to do; the National Union of Healthcare Workers filed a complaint against Kaiser in July over an algorithm for mental-health patients.
Kaiser Permanente says its AI tools do not make care decisions and support clinicians; it says its deterioration-alert tool reduced deaths by 16% in internal research published in 2020.
The article says it is unclear whether the law prohibits any current use of AI in hospitals or clinics; neither Bonta's nor the nurses association's spokespeople gave examples.

A healthcare attorney expects more malpractice suits claiming doctors over-relied on AI guidance; a separate bill giving nurses workplace protection when they override AI (AB 2575) was vetoed by Newsom.
quote_evidence: A new California law will bar hospitals and doctors’ offices from using artificial intelligence to independently perform medical tasks that require a professional license, such as prescribing medications or ordering tests.
It’s unclear if the law prohibits any current uses of artificial intelligence in hospitals or clinics.
The hospital association and the California Medical Association, representing 50,000 doctors, were neutral on the law.
why_it_matters_hint: A state law keeps licensed clinicians, not AI, responsible for licensed medical decisions from 1 Jan 2027, but its practical reach is unclear.
event_date: Law signed on or about 30 Sep 2026 (the article says 'last week'; first outlets reported it on 30 Sep 2026); Press Democrat article dated 10 Oct 2026
notes: Read the Press Democrat in full (byline Grant Stringer, Bay Area News Group). The signing date is not in the article; 30 Sep 2026 comes from search listings of other outlets' reports (National Nurses United 30 Sep, Healthcare IT News 1 Oct), which were not opened. Not carried in our editions of the last 14 days.
